$comment: RECOVERY sprint config. The decision rule below is registered BEFORE the sprint runs, on purpose — a rule written after the numbers arrive is a rule that bends to the numbers. Post IDs are filled in by hand as each reel is published manually from mobile with trending audio; /api/recovery/report reads them from here.

protocol.publishing: MANUAL from mobile, with trending audio. The Graph API cannot attach trending or licensed audio, so the pipeline deliberately stops at status 'ready'. During a recovery sprint that is an advantage, not a limitation: trending audio is a distribution lever auto-publish does not have.
protocol.time_slot: Same hour +/- 30 min for all five reels. Publishing time is NOT a tested variable in this sprint.
protocol.cadence: The existing Character Studio calendar is daily, so the five recovery reels land on consecutive days rather than the 4-5/week originally written here. Using the existing calendar was chosen deliberately over imposing a separate cadence.
protocol.stories: Unchanged. Stories keep running in normal mode to hold follower touch while reel cadence is reduced. They are not part of this test.
protocol.one_variable: Only the motion/prompt layer changes. Captions, publishing time, styling and hashtags stay exactly as they are.
protocol.qa_gate: Every reel passes the first-frame QA gate before approval: measured duration inside 5.5-7.5s (automatic, server-side), plus three manual checks — face/movement visible in frame 0, eye contact by 1.5s, no slow establishing shot.
protocol.calendar_integration: Recovery reels are ordinary chs_daily_plans reel slots in the normal Character Studio calendar, carrying a RECOVERY n/5 badge. They are approved in /review with the same button as any other day, generate through the same route, and publish through the existing /api/publish/cron. There is no second recovery workflow and no second publish cron. Slot 5 waits for the story engine to create day 100 (2026-09-08); re-run POST /api/recovery/integrate to map it.

baseline.$comment: The average of the 20.8.-1.9. window, which is what 'did this work' is measured against.

primary_kpi.$comment: Watch time is the only metric in this account's data that correlates with reach: every post above 4.5s has 250+ views, every post below 3s has under 180.

decision_rule.verdict_is_not_a_single_number: Set 2026-09-04. The branch below is the pre-registered ACTION, but it may not be read on avg_watch_time alone. A reel counts as measured only when every metric in required_report_metrics is present, and the report prints all of them next to the verdict. avg_watch_ratio in particular separates 'the reel did not hold' from 'the reel was simply short' — a distinction avg_watch_time cannot make on its own, and the reason nine ~5.2s reels looked like a creative failure when they were a length failure. None of these feed CI scoring.

context_only.$comment: Views are context, never the decision. Across a 47-242 range they are noise at n=1.

branches.action: Continue with the simple compiler. Widen the motifs gradually. CI_SCORING_FROZEN stays true for a further 14 days.
Extend the sprint by 3 more reels in the strongest direction. Change nothing else.

branches.verdict: The prompt layer was not the (only) problem.
branches.action: Next tested variable is the VISUAL MOTIF layer (summer / pool / sea / living social scenes — the approved reference direction), still through the simple compiler. One variable again.
